beats.headline: Dropped in a narrow room
beats.text: Carl has been tinkering with this bomb for a while. The first version, Just Wait Until Your Daddy Gets Home, was so big it had to have wheels; this one packs about the same punch, minus the Fear, into a device the size of a thermos, a thermobaric explosion that incinerates anything within a hundred meters. Louis has fifty of them on Party Planner, and only fifty because the explosive dust is a pain to make. The AI has helpfully called it The Waffle Maker. In Khepri's narrow temple, as Vinata's three guards leap at him, it goes off. Fwummm-bam. Only his immortality holds Carl's atoms together.

beats.headline: Liquified
beats.text: Among Carl's achievements from the raid is Liquified: while immortal, he blew himself up, dropping a bomb at his own feet. The AI loved the slow-motion replay. It only worked, it adds, because he had god-tier immortality; most versions of that spell would have splattered him into so many pieces he would never have reconstituted in time. And don't even think about trying it with that other, bigger bomb in his inventory.

beats.headline: Bombs away
beats.text: Over the target, Samantha shouts from the cockpit, every bomb aboard Louis's airship arms itself, and Carl puts Overclocked on each one. Louis calls bombs away, and several spots in the floor slide open. The square, shield- and tech-busting No Disassembles clink out of their holders first, then the round, high-yield Waffle Makers, shaped like tubes, clunking out heavier and vanishing into the freezing mist. The whole load is gone in seconds.

beats.headline: Shit Just Hit
beats.text: Carl's plan was to aim the massive-payload waffle makers at the theater housing the generator for the zarogoths. Instead, levitating up out of Larracos, he drops the entire contents of one inventory folder, titled Shit Just Hit, toward the Piccadilly: about twenty waffle makers, two no disassembles, a pair of anti-personnel cheese cutters, about five hundred impact hob-lobbers and more dynamite than he can count. His Walk on Air gives out three-quarters of the way to the edge. When the bombs hit, every window in the area shatters.
